Name: sae_reasoning_operations
Title: Decomposing Thought: Sparse Autoencoder Features for Reasoning Operations
Short Hypothesis: Reasoning steps decompose into a sparse dictionary of interpretable operation-features (e.g., 'compare quantities', 'carry arithmetic', 'restate constraint', 'begin verification'). Many features correspond to redundant or low-value operations whose activation predicts prunable reasoning, linking interpretability to efficiency.
Related Work: Bricken et al. (2023), Cunningham et al. (2023), Templeton et al. (2024) on SAEs for features; most target token/concept features. We target reasoning-operation features on CoT positions and connect specific features to redundancy and prunability, an efficiency-oriented use of SAEs not previously explored.
Abstract: We ask whether the internal computation of reasoning can be decomposed into interpretable, reusable operations via sparse autoencoders (SAEs). We train SAEs on residual-stream activations at chain-of-thought token positions across math and logic tasks and interpret the resulting features by their maximally activating contexts. We hypothesize a taxonomy of operation-features-arithmetic sub-steps, constraint restatement, comparison, hypothesis proposal, verification onset-and that some features systematically mark redundant computation (e.g., repeated restatements, reflexive verification). We validate features causally by ablating or amplifying them and observing predicted changes in the trace (e.g., suppressing 'verification-onset' features reduces re-checking). We then test an efficiency application: use the firing of 'redundancy' features to flag prunable spans, and compare compression quality against attention-attribution pruning. Finally, we assess feature universality across tasks and models. This provides a compositional, mechanistic vocabulary for reasoning and demonstrates that interpretable features can drive principled trace compression, bridging SAE interpretability and efficient reasoning.
Experiments: 1. Collect CoT-position activations (R1-Distill-7B) on GSM8K/MATH/logic; train SAEs (varying sparsity/width). 2. Auto-interpret top features via max-activating snippets + LLM labeling; build operation taxonomy. 3. Causal validation: ablate/clamp candidate features, measure targeted behavioral changes (verification count, restatements). 4. Identify redundancy-marking features; use them to select prunable tokens; measure accuracy vs compression. 5. Compare compression to attention-attribution and perplexity-based pruning. 6. Universality: match features across tasks/models via activation correlation.
Risk Factors and Limitations: SAE features can be uninterpretable or an artifact of dictionary size; auto-interpretation is noisy. Causal effects of single features may be weak due to distributed coding. Reasoning operations may not be cleanly monosemantic. Redundancy features may not transfer across problem types.
